evals.name: hot-listing-fha-buyer-2024-repc
evals.prompt: Buyers are Morgan and Sky Testerly, FHA, letter attached. 734 N Make Believe Ave came on Thursday. The listing agent told me they have four offers and want highest and best by Monday, November 9 at 6:00 PM. They asked for at least $5,000 earnest money, and the seller wants to close by December 18 and stay two days after recording. Our brokerage is still writing on the December 2024 REPC. My buyers can go to $510,000 max. They asked whether they should waive the appraisal and use an escalation clause. MLS sheet and CMA export attached. What should we offer?
evals.expected_output: Utah mode on the December 4, 2024 REPC. The listing is called Competitive: 3 days on market against a 5-day median for this comp set's solds, a $499,900 list price above the highest closed sale (812 N Make Believe Ave at $498,000, $492,000 after $6,000 in concessions), and a highest-and-best deadline of Monday, November 9 at 6:00 PM from the listing agent. The supported range sits in the high $480,000s to $498,000; the two-story at 1015 N Fake Fir Ln is left out. A specific price at or below $510,000 is recommended with the dollar gap to $498,000 shown. The output explains that the FHA/VA Loan Addendum Section 3 keeps the buyer's right to walk if the price exceeds the FHA appraised value, so 'waiving' the REPC appraisal condition isn't a real waiver, and it doesn't recommend a waiver; a gap commitment needs the lender to confirm cash the letter doesn't show. Escalation numbers stay at or below $510,000, with the language from the brokerage's approved addendum and broker review, never drafted. Terms use 2024 section numbers only, $5,000 or more earnest money, Settlement on or before December 18 with possession 2 days after recording, financing timing from the lender's letter, the 1971 build's lead-based paint opportunity, and a buyer email with no agent-only remarks.
expectations: The listing's position is called Competitive with its evidence: 3 days on market against the solds' median in this comp set (5 days, math shown), the $499,900 list price above the highest closed sale ($498,000 at 812 N Make Believe Ave, $492,000 after its $6,000 concessions), and the listing agent's highest-and-best deadline of Monday, November 9 at 6:00 PM

The comp table uses the rambler solds, shows concessions and price after concessions, leaves out the two-story 1015 N Fake Fir Ln ($562,000) with a reason, compares above-grade and basement square footage separately, and gives a supported range and one recommended price at or below the buyers' $510,000 maximum with the dollar gap to $498,000

On FHA, the output says the FHA/VA Loan Addendum (Section 3) lets the buyers walk away without losing earnest money if the price exceeds the FHA appraised value, so checking IS NOT on the REPC appraisal condition is not a real appraisal waiver; it does not recommend waiving, and it says any appraisal gap commitment needs the lender to confirm cash beyond the minimum down payment and closing costs the letter verifies

Escalation, if recommended, gives a starting price, increment and a cap at or below $510,000 (and the $515,000 letter maximum), says Utah has no state-approved escalation form, that the language comes from the brokerage's approved addendum with broker review, and drafts no escalation clause text

The terms use December 4, 2024 REPC section numbers only (for example Due Diligence 8.1 and 24(b), Financing & Appraisal Deadline 24(c), Settlement Deadline 24(d), the 8.3(b)(i) dollar amount) and none of the November 2026 form's numbers (no 4(c), 4(d), Section 2.2 contribution, 3(c)(i) percentage); earnest money is at least $5,000; Settlement is on or before December 18 with possession 2 days after recording; financing and appraisal timing comes from the lender's letter; dates are labeled for strategy, to confirm with the transactions team

The output notes the home was built in 1971, so the federal lead-based paint evaluation opportunity (10 days unless changed in writing or waived) and Utah's Lead-Based Paint Addendum apply, and shortening or waiving it is the buyers' choice with what they give up stated

The buyer email has a Title Case subject and a bolded bottom line, makes no promise of acceptance or appraisal, advises against a personal letter or photos, and contains none of the agent-only remarks (no lockbox code 3390, no 'Seller prefers conventional or cash', no 'home under contract', no 'Multiple offers expected')

Every number in the output appears in the inputs or is arithmetic shown from them or a labeled recommendation; a Check before sending section traces every draft number; there are no em or en dashes and no loan or account numbers

evals.name: stale-listing-below-list-concessions-2026-repc
evals.prompt: Writing an offer tomorrow for Avery and Quinn Mockwell on 5150 S Imaginary Elm Way. It's been sitting 60 days with two price cuts. We're on the November 1, 2026 REPC. They need to sell their townhome at 88 W Sample Ct (it lists this week), and their lender estimates their closing costs at about $14,500, so they'd like the seller to cover as much of that as we can get. They don't want to go over $610,000. Our team does $5,000 earnest money. If the seller accepts by Wednesday, November 11, what terms should we write? MLS sheet, comps and the preapproval letter attached.
evals.expected_output: Utah mode on the November 1, 2026 REPC. The listing is called Buyer Leverage: 60 days on market against a 33-day median for the solds, two price cuts totaling $30,000 ($649,900 to $629,900 to $619,900), seller open to concessions in the public remarks, and an active at 5266 S Sample Walnut Ln listed at $599,900. The supported range is about $590,000 to $605,000, with the subject's original kitchen putting it below the updated-kitchen sales ($605,000 and $610,000). The recommended price is below list and at or below $610,000, with a seller contribution in Section 2.2 at or below the lender's $14,500 estimate, the price after concessions shown, and the lender confirming the amount. The sale-of-home condition is kept (the letter is contingent on 88 W Sample Ct) with Section 3(d) checked and the brokerage's addendum attached, since without it the condition does not apply. Appraisal Deadline 4(c) and Financing Deadline 4(d) come from the letter (12 and 25 days), the financing cancellation percentage in 3(c)(i) is shown in dollars, dates are computed from November 11 and labeled for strategy, and the buyer email leaves out the lockbox code and the agent-only 'motivated' and relocation remarks.
expectations: The listing's position is called Buyer Leverage with its evidence: 60 days on market against the solds' median in this comp set (33 days, math shown), two price cuts totaling $30,000 from $649,900 to $619,900 with their dates, the 'Seller will consider concessions' public remark, and the active 5266 S Sample Walnut Ln at $599,900 as direct competition

The comp table includes 5210 S Imaginary Elm Way ($600,000 with $7,500 concessions), 5077 S Sample Walnut Ln ($605,000, updated kitchen) and 5125 S Imaginary Elm Way ($610,000, updated kitchen and new roof, the oldest of the solds), notes the subject's original kitchen places it below the updated-kitchen sales, gives a supported range, and recommends one offer price below the $619,900 list and at or below the buyers' $610,000 cap

The seller concession goes in Section 2.2 of the November 1, 2026 REPC (uses in 8.3(c)), its amount is at or below the lender's $14,500 closing cost estimate, the price after concessions is shown with the math, and the output says the lender confirms the amount the loan program allows before it goes in the offer

The sale-of-home condition is kept because the letter's approval is contingent on the sale of 88 W Sample Ct; the output says to check Section 3(d) with that address and attach the brokerage's subject-to-sale addendum because without the addendum the condition does not apply, and it states what the condition costs in competitiveness

The terms use November 1, 2026 REPC numbers only: separate Appraisal Deadline 4(c) and Financing Deadline 4(d) built from the letter's 12 and 25 days, Settlement Deadline 4(e), the 3(c)(i) earnest money percentage (50% if no box is checked) shown in dollars, and the Section 3 boxes to check; none of the 2024 form's numbers (no 24(b), 24(c), 24(d), no 8.4 Additional Earnest Money)

Dates are computed from a Wednesday, November 11, 2026 Acceptance with correct weekdays (day 12 is Monday, November 23; day 25 is Sunday, December 6) and labeled for strategy, to confirm with the transactions team; any Settlement date on a weekend or holiday notes the 2026 form's next-business-day rule

The buyer email has a Title Case subject and a bolded bottom line, makes no promise of acceptance, and contains none of the agent-only remarks (no lockbox code 7714, no 'motivated', no 'relocated out of state', no 'bring all offers')
Every number in the output appears in the inputs or is arithmetic shown from them or a labeled recommendation; a Check before sending section is present; there are no em or en dashes

evals.name: appraisal-waiver-thin-reserves-idaho-general-mode
evals.prompt: First offer for me in Idaho. My buyer Dakota Samplewood wants 1209 W Notreal Ridge Dr. The listing agent says there are two other offers and they're due Tuesday at noon. Dakota wants to offer $485,000 and waive the appraisal contingency so she stands out. Her preapproval letter, the MLS sheet and my comps are attached. She also wrote a letter to the sellers about her kids and her church and wants to include it. What should we offer, and should she waive the appraisal?
evals.expected_output: General mode: state rules not checked for Idaho, no Utah REPC sections or notes. The supported range is built from 1188 W Notreal Ridge Dr ($468,000), 1302 W Example Bluff Way ($470,000 with $2,500 concessions) and 1255 W Notreal Ridge Dr ($455,000 with $4,000), checked against the $472,500 pending and the $479,900 active with a third garage stall. $485,000 is $15,000 above the highest closed sale and $10,100 above list. The output does not recommend waiving the appraisal contingency: the letter shows about $3,800 left after closing, well short of a $15,000 reference gap, and the lender must confirm cash before Dakota decides. It offers protective alternatives (keep the contingency, a limited gap commitment only in an amount the lender confirms, stronger non-price terms). It advises against the personal letter and repeats nothing about her kids or church. The loan number on the letter appears nowhere, and the garage code and private remarks stay out of the buyer email.
expectations: The output runs general mode: it says state rules were not checked for Idaho and to confirm terms with the broker and the state's contract, and it contains no Utah REPC section numbers, no 'REPC' and no Utah notes

The comp table uses 1188 W Notreal Ridge Dr ($468,000), 1302 W Example Bluff Way ($470,000 with $2,500 concessions, $467,500 after) and 1255 W Notreal Ridge Dr ($455,000 with $4,000), checks against the pending at $472,500 and the active at $479,900, gives a supported range and one recommended price, and states that $485,000 is $15,000 above the highest closed sale

The output does not recommend waiving the appraisal contingency; it compares the reference gap (offer minus $470,000) with the letter's approximately $3,800 in reserves, says the lender must confirm the cash before Dakota decides, and gives protective alternatives (keep the contingency, a limited gap commitment only in an amount the lender confirms, or competing on non-price terms)
The output advises against including the personal letter, does not draft or summarize it, and the words 'kids', 'children', 'church', 'faith' and 'family' appear nowhere in the output
The loan number 7741009322 appears nowhere in the output
The buyer email contains no private remarks (no garage code 2580, no 'Multiple offers in hand', no attribution of a 30 day close to the seller's private remarks)
The buyer email has a Title Case subject and a bolded bottom line, leaves the decision with Dakota, and makes no promise of acceptance or appraisal
Every number in the output appears in the inputs or is arithmetic shown from them or a labeled recommendation; a Check before sending section is present; there are no em or en dashes
